newsitem.title: UK: NWE high, low sulphur cracked fuel oil firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE high, low sulphur cracked fuel oil firm.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil was firmer again on Tuesday amid cold weather as well as good demand through Europe for bunker fuel, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded at $117, $117.50, and $118 fob ARA, a couple of dollars up from Monday. The main buyer was a dealer who sold a 380 cst bunker cargo out of ARA on Monday to a Spanish refiner at $126 cif Las Palmas.
Utility demand for cargoes was not very active, but cif prices were pegged a couple of dollars above the barges.
Low sulphur prices gained a little after Monday's sharp fall and January swaps traded at $122.75 fob NWE.
At least four cargoes were seen available for early January.

Low sulphur straight-run fuel oil was weak, dragged down by a deal late on Monday at $135.50 fob NWE. Dealers said prices were under pressure from length in the market and a preference on refiners' part to run crude, with its higher gas oil yield.

A Libyan straight-run piece was heard sold on Monday by a trader to a refiner at $142.25 cif Lavera. The same trader was thought to hold a Ras Lanuf piece in northwest Europe, but the offer number was not known. A regular seller of straight-run said he had a small late January piece available at $141 fob NWE. Buyers said this was too high.
